Bitis gabonica is a large, heavily built viperid snake inhabiting the rainforests and woodlands of sub-Saharan Africa. This striking ontogenetic increase in body size is accompanied by a correspondingly dramatic gain in mass; neonatal individuals typically possess a wet weight of about 52 grams [Wwb = about 52 grams] at the point of eclosion. Such a small initial mass stands in stark contrast to the ultimate wet weight recorded for reproductively active adult females, which may reach as much as 11,300 grams [Wwi = as much as 11,300 grams], illustrating the profound energetic investment required to complete somatic growth across the species’ extended life history.
